newsitem.title: GERMANY: Cathay Pacific cuts fares from Germany.
newsitem.headline: Cathay Pacific cuts fares from Germany.

text.p: Cathay Pacific said on Tuesday that it has cut economy class fares from Germany to Hong Kong by nearly ten percent to match lower prices from Deutsche Lufthansa AG and Air France.

Michael Gabrielli, Cathay Pacific passenger sales and marketing manager Germany, said the airline reduced the economy class fare from Frankfurt to Hong Kong to 1,849 marks from 2,049 marks after Lufthansa cut its price to that level.
Gabrielli told a news conference in Frankfurt that pressure on air fares in Germany is increasing even though passenger levels to the British colony are rising.
"There are too many special offers on the market, yields are falling and prices have fallen, especially in economy," he said.

Gabrielli said he could not understand why state-subsidised airlines such as Air France were offering cheap deals when market conditions did not require this, although he did not cite Air France price levels.
"We had double-figure growth in the first half of this year. Hong Kong is an "in" place, everyone wants to go there and that has boosted demand," he said.

Cathay saw its passenger levels for Germany stagnate at more than 100,000 last year, while revenue topped 100 million marks and a load factor of 72 per cent was achieved on the daily Frankfurt-Hong Kong flight, he added.
Gabrielli said the airline would offer tour operators and ticket consolidators joint prices with Singapore Airlines allowing travellers to fly with both airlines throughout Asia.
Combined prices had already been offered for flights to Hong Kong via Singapore since February, he noted.
Cathay said it has a 50-50 mix of business and leisure travellers out of Germany, with about 65 percent travelling in economy class.
